short: (2+1)D front end (M06) is standard: established in lip reading, ported to ultrasound; a 6.3% MSE edge over CNN+LSTM, one speaker, one run; MSE-only evaluation (M12 behind).
position: The paper [@toth2020threed] changes the image front end (M06): a (2+1)D convolution over five ultrasound frames sampled with stride 6, a 25-frame span that the authors put at about 300 ms. The authors credit video action recognition and earlier 3D CNNs (Sec. 1–2). M06 is standard, not ahead: spatiotemporal convolution was established in lip reading by 2017 [@assael2016lipnet; @stafylakis2017combining], and a [concurrent] ultrasound-to-formant network split part of its 3D convolution into parallel 2D spatial and 1D temporal branches [@saha2020ultra2speech]. The headline win over CNN+LSTM is small and unrepeated: test MSE 0.336 to 0.315, 6.3% relative (inference), one speaker, one run, against a baseline the authors retrained with changed input and output sizes. The original CNN+LSTM took 32-frame chunks (Sec. 5), so context width confounds only the gains over the one-frame FCN and 2D CNN (Sec. 4). Evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work: MSE and R² of 13 vocoder parameters only, while the group's own earlier studies of the same speaker ran MUSHRA listening tests [@csapo2017dnn; @grosz2018f0].
